hero.title: Sheffield Quantum
hero.subtitle: From Atom-like Systems to Scalable Devices.

introParagraphs: Welcome to SQIL at the University of Sheffield. We are a new research group focused on creating useful applications from physics experiments by injecting advanced engineering technologies.

Our core mission is to answer whether single atom-like defects in solids can be controlled at scale. We borrow tools from existing semiconductor processing, combining silicon photonics, microwave electronics, and robotics to build custom, large-scale quantum systems.

pillars.title: Silicon Photonics
pillars.desc: Embedding atom-like systems in photonic nanocavities.

pillars.title: Microwave Electronics
pillars.desc: Scalable control using multi-layer silicon electronics.

pillars.title: Spin Physics
pillars.desc: Spin-photon interfaces for quantum computing networks.

pillars.title: Robotics & Sensing
pillars.desc: High-resolution sensing aligning large vector fields.

researchPage.intro: We put photonics and electronics front and centre: with useful applications in adding spins to photonic quantum computing and networks, but also for more near-term implications for high resolution quantum sensing.

sections.title: Integrated Photonics
sections.body: We design new photonic nanocavities and demonstrate compatibility with silicon photonics. Recent work has looked at embedding atom-like systems directly into these scalable photonic circuits.

sections.title: Scalable Electronics
sections.body: Engineering applied to spins through scalable microwave control using multi-layer silicon electronics. We borrow techniques from classical semiconductor processing to control quantum defects at scale.

sections.title: Robotics & Sensing
sections.body: Advancing quantum sensing by aligning large vector fields with custom-built robotics. We build large-scale confocal microscopes to automate the characterization of quantum devices.
